title: How do sign languages work?
examples: Is sign language the same everywhere?
What are the parts of a sign?
Is sign language a real language?

parts.ask: What are the parts of a sign?

explain.say: Imagine telling a whole story, with jokes and questions, without making a sound. Millions of Deaf people do that every day using sign languages. Look at the person on the board. Every sign is built from a few parts. The first is the handshape: a fist, a flat hand, one finger up.

parts.label: Face
parts.ask: Why do signers use facial expressions?

explain.say: Next, see the location, the place on the body where you make the sign, like the chin or the chest. The same handshape in a different place can mean something different! Can you think of a gesture you make near your face?

parts.label: Face
parts.ask: Why do signers use facial expressions?

explain.say: Now look at the movement and the palm direction: how the hand moves, and which way your palm faces. A small change can change the meaning, just like changing one letter in a word. Try waving with your palm in, then out. Does it feel different?

parts.label: Handshape
parts.ask: What are the parts of a sign?

parts.label: Location
parts.note: Where the sign is made on the body.

parts.label: Face
parts.ask: Why do signers use facial expressions?

explain.say: Look at the face on the board. Facial expressions are part of the grammar: raised eyebrows can turn a sign into a yes or no question. Try asking a question with just your eyebrows!

explain.say: Wonderful! For names, signers often fingerspell, one handshape for each letter. Look at the board: h, a, n, d. Sign languages also differ: British, American and Indian Sign Language are all different. Wow: in Nicaragua, Deaf children created a new sign language in the 1980s! Challenge: learn to fingerspell your name.

faq.q: What are the parts of a sign?
faq.a: A sign is built from handshape, location, movement and palm direction, plus facial expression. Change one part and you can change the meaning.

faq.q: Why do signers use facial expressions?
faq.a: In sign languages the face is part of the grammar. Raised eyebrows can mark a yes or no question, and the mouth can show size or manner.
asks: Is the face part of sign language?

faq.q: Is sign language the same everywhere?
faq.a: No. There are about 300 sign languages. British Sign Language and American Sign Language are very different, and Indian Sign Language is different again.

faq.q: Is sign language a real language?
faq.a: Yes. Sign languages have their own words, grammar and jokes, and children learn them naturally, just like spoken languages. They are not just gestures for English.
Fingerspelling uses a handshape for each letter to spell out names and new words. British Sign Language uses two hands for its alphabet; American Sign Language uses one.
asks: How do you spell in sign language?

facts: There are around 300 different sign languages in the world.
British Sign Language uses a two-handed alphabet, while American Sign Language uses a one-handed alphabet.
Nicaraguan Sign Language was created by Deaf children at schools in Nicaragua in the 1970s and 1980s.
